text: Which series of models is OpenAI best known for developing?
options: The GPT series of large language models
The Claude series of large language models
The Gemini series of large language models
The Llama series of large language models
answer: The GPT series of large language models
explanation: GPT stands for generative pre-trained transformer, and the name has been carried through the whole line since the original 2018 model. The other three series on this list belong to Anthropic, Google and Meta, which is a quick way to rule three options out and check the fourth.
answerAliases: generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) series of large language models

text: Anthropic and OpenAI are both headquartered in the same American city. Which city?
explanation: Both are public benefit corporations registered and based in San Francisco, and both were founded by people who had just left the same organisation. The overlap in people, funding and hiring is the single largest structural fact about the frontier lab industry.

text: Which French AI company, founded in 2023 and based in Paris, is known for open weight language models?
explanation: Mistral released the Mixtral mixture of experts model under an Apache licence, which was the first genuinely competitive open weight model from a European lab. The valuation above 14 billion dollars makes it the most valuable European AI company.

text: Which Hangzhou based AI company develops open weight models and is owned and funded by a hedge fund?
explanation: DeepSeek is funded by High-Flyer, which is unusual, since it means the research is not being driven by outside investors looking for a return. Their reasoning models made strong performance on math and code benchmarks at unusually low cost, and the models were released with open weights.
answerAliases: Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Basic Technology Research Co., Ltd.

text: Which Seattle based non-profit research institute was founded in 2014 by Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen?
explanation: Ai2, as it styles itself, was built to do open research rather than to ship products, and the distinction matters. The Allen Institute for Brain Science is a separate organisation in Seattle that studies neural tissue, and the two are easy to mix up because they share a name and a benefactor.

source.title: Allen Institute for AI
source.label: Allen Institute for AI on Wikipedia

text: Which lab was founded in 2010, acquired by Google in 2014, and later merged with Google Brain in 2023?
explanation: DeepMind was founded in London and became the company behind AlphaGo, AlphaFold and Gemini. Google paid a reported 400 million pounds for it, and the merge with Google Brain in April 2023 is what created the awkward situation of two research groups with the same name inside one company.

text: Which Toronto based company focuses on large language models for regulated industries such as banking and healthcare?
explanation: Aidan Gomez, Ivan Zhang and Nick Frosst founded Cohere in 2019, and Gomez was also the first author of the transformer paper that everything modern is built on. The pitch is deployment inside regulated companies rather than a consumer chatbot, which is a slower business with far fewer users.

text: In which year did Google merge DeepMind with its Google Brain division to form Google DeepMind?
explanation: Google had already bought DeepMind in 2014, and for nine years it and Google Brain ran as separate organisations with overlapping goals. The 2023 merge left one research lab with a duplicated name inside it, which is a fairly ordinary outcome of acquisitions and an unusually visible one here.

text: Which lab develops the Claude family of AI models?
explanation: Claude is the flagship product of Anthropic, the public benefit corporation founded in January 2021 by former OpenAI members including Dario and Daniela Amodei with an explicit AI safety mission. OpenAI is the tempting wrong answer because the Amodeis came from there, but OpenAI builds the GPT series, not Claude.

text: Which lab develops the Gemini family of AI models?
explanation: Google DeepMind is responsible for the proprietary Gemini family alongside the open-weight Gemma models, after Google merged DeepMind with the Google Brain division in April 2023. OpenAI is the closest distractor since GPT and Gemini compete head to head, but GPT belongs to OpenAI.

text: Which lab develops the Llama family of AI models?
explanation: Meta AI is the research division behind the Llama models, which Meta released with open weights and built its Meta AI assistant on. Mistral AI is the natural confusion because the Paris lab also publishes open-weight models, but its family is Mistral and Mixtral, not Llama.

text: Which former OpenAI chief scientist co-founded Safe Superintelligence Inc.?
explanation: Ilya Sutskever founded SSI with Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy after leaving OpenAI in May 2024, with a mission focused on building safe superintelligence. Sam Altman is the closest distractor as the OpenAI CEO whose brief removal preceded Sutskever's exit, but Altman stayed and Sutskever left to start SSI.

text: Which former OpenAI chief technology officer founded Thinking Machines Lab in 2025?
explanation: Mira Murati, OpenAI's former chief technology officer, founded Thinking Machines Lab in February 2025 as a San Francisco public benefit corporation. Ilya Sutskever is the tempting alternative because he also left OpenAI to found a lab, but his lab is SSI, founded a year earlier.

text: What does World Labs, the startup founded by Fei-Fei Li, build?
options: AI accelerator chips for data centers
explanation: World Labs came out of stealth in September 2024 with $230 million in funding to build large world models that perceive and interact with the 3D world, aimed at artists, designers and game studios. Protein folding is DeepMind's AlphaFold territory, while Li's bet is that spatial intelligence is the frontier after language.

text: Which AI lab was created by Google LaMDA developers Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas?
explanation: Shazeer and De Freitas built LaMDA at Google, then left to found Character.ai, whose beta opened in September 2022 with customizable characters that users define and publish. Inflection AI is the closest distractor because it is also a chatbot lab, but its product was Pi and its founders came from DeepMind, not LaMDA.

text: In August 2026, Google handed day-to-day leadership of Google DeepMind to a 13-year veteran of the lab, who took the new title of senior vice-president. Which veteran?
explanation: Google's own memo announced that Koray Kavukcuoglu would step up as SVP of Google DeepMind, while Demis Hassabis gave up day-to-day operations to become chair of GDM and chief scientist of Alphabet. Kavukcuoglu had already been the lab's CTO and Google's chief AI architect. Oriol Vinyals is the tempting wrong answer because he was a DeepMind research VP at the time, but he left Google days later to co-found Discovery Loop.

source.label: Sundar Pichai and Demis Hassabis on the Google DeepMind leadership change

text: In August 2026, Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le left Google together to found a new research lab. Which lab?
explanation: Discovery Loop is a Palo Alto public benefit corporation whose stated goal is automating the propose-run-evaluate loop of scientific research, starting with machine learning itself. Google stayed in as a founding investor and cloud partner, so losing four researchers turned into an equity position. Ineffable Intelligence is the tempting wrong answer because it is the other ex-DeepMind lab that raised over a billion dollars, but David Silver founded that one months earlier.

text: In the six days from June 18 to June 24, 2026, four senior Google DeepMind researchers said or were reported to be leaving for rival labs, and three of the four headed for the same company. Which company?
explanation: John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold, announced first, and Gemini contributors Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel followed within days. Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer was the only one of the four who chose OpenAI, less than two years after Google paid billions to bring him back from Character.AI. Both OpenAI and Anthropic were close to going public, which is what made pre-IPO equity worth swapping a stable job for.

source.label: TechCrunch on the June 2026 Google departures

text: In July 2026, Thinking Machines Lab co-founder Lilian Weng announced she was stepping down citing her health, then rejoined which lab two days later?
explanation: Weng ran OpenAI's safety organisation before leaving in November 2024 to co-found Thinking Machines with Mira Murati, and she went back to lead a team supporting recursive self-improvement research. Murati stayed at her own lab, which is why the return looked awkward two days after the resignation note. Anthropic is the tempting wrong answer because it is Thinking Machines' most direct competitor.

text: In August 2026, Nvidia's vice president of AI research left the company after eight years to found a Toronto startup building world models so robots can train inside simulation. Which researcher was that?
explanation: Fidler ran Nvidia's Toronto spatial intelligence lab and was part of the team behind its Cosmos world model before announcing her departure. Her co-founders are Zan Gojcic, the former Nvidia research director in Zurich who is now CTO, and Huan Ling, her former doctoral student who is chief scientist. David Silver is the tempting wrong answer because he is the other ex-DeepMind founder with a billion-dollar lab, but his company is Ineffable Intelligence.

text: In August 2026, the researcher who led Alibaba's Qwen model family founded a new AI lab in Shanghai. Which lab did he start?
explanation: Junyang Lin left Alibaba in March 2026 with a post reading 'Bye my beloved Qwen', then named his new Shanghai lab after pragmatics, the study of meaning in context, which is roughly what an agent has to do. Zhipu AI is the tempting wrong answer because it is one of the best-known Chinese labs shipping open-weight models, but it has nothing to do with Lin. The Shanghai AI Laboratory is a real institute too, but a state-backed research body rather than a founder-led startup.

source.label: RuntimeWire on Junyang Lin's Pragmatik Labs

text: In July 2026, Richard Sutton and his former student Khurram Javed left John Carmack's Keen Technologies to found a new lab in Toronto. What did they call it?
explanation: Sutton, who shared the 2024 Turing Award for founding modern reinforcement learning, started Oak Lab to build agents that keep learning after deployment. His stated target is an agent with a trillion parameters that learns and plans in real time on about 20 watts, roughly human-brain power. Skyfall AI is the tempting wrong answer because it launched from Toronto in the same month, but it came from the Maluuba founders.

source.label: The Decoder on Oak Lab's launch

text: In August 2026, a Princeton-rooted research lab for scientific computing came out of stealth with a $10.6 million round led by Dimension. Which of its three founders had previously co-founded the Wolfram Physics Project?
explanation: Gorard is an applied mathematician who co-founded the Wolfram Physics Project with Stephen Wolfram and now runs Lanyon as CEO. His co-founders are Ammar Hakim, the computational physicist who is CTO, and James Juno, the plasma physicist. Ammar Hakim is the tempting wrong answer because he is the better-known senior scientist of the pair, but the Wolfram connection is Gorard's.

source.label: Physical AI News on Lanyon AI's founding team

text: In August 2026, which US chipmaker unveiled its own long-horizon research lab, headquartered in Boise, Idaho?
explanation: Micron Research Labs is a planned ten billion dollar research campus in Boise that will host hundreds of researchers working on memory and AI, with construction slated to begin in 2027. Nvidia is the tempting wrong answer because it is by far the largest AI chip company, but this is the American memory maker building for its own next decade alongside its two new Boise fabs.

source.label: Engineering News-Record on Micron Research Labs

text: In July 2026, the LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman and the Zynga founder Mark Pincus were reported to be backing a new research lab focused on computer-use models. Which lab?
explanation: Prentis launched in April 2026 with serial entrepreneur Ritankar Das as CEO and trains models inside real office workflows rather than on web-scale text. Manas AI is the tempting wrong answer because it is Hoffman's own drug-discovery startup, which he went into founder mode on after leaving Microsoft's board. Inflection AI is the other lab he co-founded, back in 2022.

text: Sakana AI, the Tokyo lab co-founded by Transformer paper co-author Llion Jones, takes its name from the Japanese word for what?
explanation: Sakana AI's name is simply the Japanese word for fish, chosen by founders David Ha, Llion Jones and Ren Ito in 2023. Crane and blossom are the classic Japanese symbols a Tokyo lab might have picked for its brand, but the actual namesake is the fish.

text: In April 2016, OpenAI released a public beta of which platform for developing and comparing reinforcement-learning algorithms?
explanation: OpenAI Gym was the April 2016 public beta, a toolkit of environments and benchmarks that became the standard interface for reinforcement-learning research. Universe is the trap because OpenAI did ship that games platform too, but it arrived in December 2016, and Stable Baselines and RLlib are libraries built on top of the Gym ecosystem rather than OpenAI's own beta.

text: Baidu's chatbot, built on its ERNIE models and launched to the public in 2023, was originally released under which Chinese name?
explanation: Ernie Bot launched as Wenxin Yiyan (文心一言), which translates roughly as 'a word from the heart', and Baidu later shortened the name to Wenxiaoyan in September 2024. Tongyi Qianwen is the trap because that is the Chinese name of Alibaba's Qwen family, and Hunyuan belongs to Tencent.

text: AI21 Labs, the Israeli maker of the Jurassic language models, was founded in which city in 2017?
explanation: Amnon Shashua, Yoav Shoham and Ori Goshen founded AI21 Labs in Tel Aviv in November 2017 and later opened a US office while keeping the Israeli base. Jerusalem is the tempting miss because Shashua is a Hebrew University professor, but the company itself is Tel Aviv's.

text: Which Beijing lab's Kimi assistant became famous for very long context windows?
explanation: Moonshot AI, founded in 2023, marketed Kimi on context windows reaching into the hundreds of thousands of tokens when rivals offered far less. Zhipu AI is the natural confusion because it is another Beijing lab shipping open-weight models, but its family is GLM, not Kimi. Founder Yang Zhilin came from Tsinghua by way of CMU.

text: Which lab, spun out of Tsinghua University, develops the GLM model family starting with ChatGLM?
explanation: Zhipu grew out of Tsinghua's knowledge-engineering group and released ChatGLM as one of China's first strong open bilingual models. Moonshot AI is the tempting answer as the other famous Beijing open-weight lab, but Kimi is theirs and GLM is Zhipu's. The Wikipedia article lives under the company's newer name, Z.ai.

text: The Allen Institute for AI, the open-model nonprofit abbreviated Ai2, is headquartered in which US city?
explanation: Paul Allen founded the institute in 2014 and it has been based in Seattle ever since, later adding an office in Tel Aviv. San Francisco is the tempting answer because that is where most AI labs cluster, but Ai2 stayed in Allen's home city of Seattle.

source.title: Allen Institute for AI
source.label: Allen Institute for AI on Wikipedia

text: Which company's enterprise model family is called Command, including Command R?
explanation: Cohere, co-founded by transformer paper co-author Aidan Gomez, sells the Command family for retrieval-augmented enterprise work rather than running a consumer chatbot. Mistral AI is the tempting answer as the other open-weight enterprise lab, but its family is Mistral and Mixtral. Command R was built for grounding answers in company documents.

text: Which pair of siblings co-founded Anthropic in 2021 after leaving OpenAI?
explanation: Dario and Daniela Amodei left OpenAI in 2020 over safety disagreements and founded Anthropic as a public benefit corporation the next January. Altman and Brockman are the tempting answer because they stayed behind to run OpenAI, which is exactly the split that defines the frontier-lab rivalry. Claude is named for Claude Shannon, not for either founder.

text: DeepSeek, the company behind the DeepSeek-R1 model, became an independent business in which month and year?
explanation: High-Flyer, the quantitative hedge fund, announced an AGI research lab in April 2023 and spun it off as the independent company DeepSeek on 17 July 2023. April 2023 is the trap because that is when the lab was announced inside High-Flyer, and January 2025 is when the R1 model arrived, not the company.

text: In which year did Elon Musk found xAI, the lab behind Grok?
explanation: Musk announced xAI in July 2023, five years after leaving OpenAI's board, and released Grok months later. 2022 is the tempting answer because that was the ChatGPT shockwave year, but xAI came the summer after. Grok takes its name from Heinlein's Stranger in a Strange Land.

text: Which lab's co-founder Mustafa Suleyman left in 2024 to run Microsoft AI, taking most of the staff with him?
explanation: Suleyman co-founded Inflection in 2022 after leaving DeepMind, then Microsoft hired him along with most of the team in what everyone called an acquihire. Character.ai is the tempting answer because Google did a similar reverse-acquihire of its founders months later, but Suleyman's lab was Inflection. Its chatbot Pi played the friendly companion, not the search box.

text: Which AI search lab was founded in 2022 by former OpenAI researcher Aravind Srinivas?
explanation: Srinivas started Perplexity to answer questions with cited sources instead of ten blue links, and it became the defining AI search product. You.com is the tempting answer because it also wraps search in AI answers, but it was founded earlier by Richard Socher. Srinivas previously worked on transformers at OpenAI and Google.

text: Which company was founded in 2016 by Clement Delangue, Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf?
explanation: The trio started Hugging Face as a chatbot app, then pivoted to the Transformers library and model hub that now hosts millions of models. Weights and Biases is the tempting answer as another beloved ML tooling company, but it does experiment tracking, not model hosting. The name and logo come from the hugging-face emoji.

text: Which Beijing lab did investor and former Google China chief Kai-Fu Lee found in 2023?
explanation: Lee launched 01.AI in March 2023 and reached unicorn valuation within months on the strength of his name alone. Moonshot AI is the tempting answer as the other famous 2023 Beijing lab, but that was Yang Zhilin's, not Lee's. Lee previously ran Google China and wrote the book AI Superpowers.

text: DeepSeek and Alibaba are both headquartered in which Chinese city?
explanation: Both the hedge-fund-backed DeepSeek and the e-commerce giant Alibaba sit in Hangzhou, home of deep Zhejiang University talent. Beijing is the tempting answer because Baidu, ByteDance and 01.AI cluster there, but Hangzhou is China's other AI pole. Alibaba's Xixi campus anchors the city's west side.

text: Who co-founded DeepMind in 2010 alongside Shane Legg and Mustafa Suleyman?
explanation: Hassabis, a former chess prodigy and game designer, founded DeepMind to solve general intelligence and sold it to Google in 2014. Geoffrey Hinton is the tempting answer as the other giant of deep learning, but he stayed in academia until joining Google separately. Hassabis later shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold.

text: Tencent, developer of the Hunyuan models, is headquartered in which city?
explanation: Tencent has sat in Shenzhen, just across the border from Hong Kong, since its 1998 founding around the QQ messenger. Guangzhou is the tempting answer as the nearby provincial capital, but Tencent's towers define Shenzhen's Nanshan district. Its WeChat app now serves over a billion users from that same city.

text: Which Beijing company founded by Zhang Yiming runs the Seed team behind the Doubao models?
explanation: Zhang Yiming founded ByteDance in 2012, and its Seed team builds Doubao, one of China's most-used AI assistants. Baidu is the tempting answer as Beijing's other AI giant, but its family is ERNIE. Doubao is little known abroad despite its enormous domestic user base.

text: In which year was OpenAI founded?
explanation: OpenAI was founded in December 2015 as a nonprofit by Altman, Musk, Sutskever and others pledging a billion dollars. 2019 is the tempting answer because that is when it created the capped-profit arm, but the lab itself dates to 2015. Musk left the board three years later, in 2018.

text: In which year was Safe Superintelligence Inc. founded by Ilya Sutskever?
explanation: Sutskever founded SSI in June 2024, weeks after leaving OpenAI, with Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy. 2023 is the tempting answer because that was the year of the OpenAI board crisis, but SSI came the following summer. The startup announced a single goal, safe superintelligence, with no product roadmap at all.

text: In February 2026, which company acquired Elon Musk's xAI in an all-stock deal?
explanation: SpaceX acquired xAI on 2 February 2026 in an all-stock deal that valued xAI at $250 billion and folded it in as a wholly owned subsidiary, later rebranded SpaceXAI. Tesla is the tempting answer because Musk also runs it, but the buyer was SpaceX. X Corp. is the same pair in the reverse direction: xAI acquired the social media company in 2025.

text: Which company announced an agreement in 2026 to acquire Hugging Face for about $12.9 billion?
explanation: Nvidia announced the roughly $12.9 billion agreement to buy Hugging Face in September 2026, promising to keep the platform open and its brand intact. Google is the tempting miss because it joined Hugging Face's 2023 funding round, but the acquirer is the GPU maker whose hardware trains most of the models the Hub hosts.

text: Which independent San Francisco lab founded by David Holz builds the Midjourney image generator?
explanation: Holz, who previously founded the Leap Motion startup, bootstrapped Midjourney with no venture funding and runs it through Discord. Ideogram is the tempting answer because it was also founded by ex-Google image researchers, but Midjourney is Holz's independent lab. Its self-funded profits made it the rare AI lab that never needed a giant's money.

text: Which volunteer research collective released the open GPT-Neo and GPT-J models in 2021?
explanation: EleutherAI organized on Discord to replicate GPT-3 in the open, releasing GPT-Neo and the 6-billion-parameter GPT-J. BigScience is the tempting answer as another open collective, but its model was BLOOM, built with Hugging Face. The name nods to the Greek word for freedom.

text: Which company's researchers created the StyleGAN family of image generators?
explanation: Nvidia's Tero Karras and colleagues released StyleGAN in 2018, and its synthetic faces powered the viral This Person Does Not Exist site. Adobe is the tempting answer because it owns image editing, but StyleGAN came from the GPU maker's research lab. Karras built it on the progressive-growing technique his team had published the year before.

text: Who founded Meta's Fundamental AI Research (FAIR) lab in 2013?
explanation: LeCun joined Meta, then Facebook, in 2013 to start FAIR while keeping his NYU post, and the lab later produced PyTorch and Llama. Hinton is the tempting answer as the other great convnet pioneer, but he went to Google, not Meta. Bengio stayed at MILA in Montreal while his two co-laureates picked sides.

text: In 2012, which Google research team trained a neural network on 10 million YouTube images that learned to recognize cats without being taught?
explanation: The Brain project, then working inside Google X before becoming a named division, trained the network on 10 million YouTube frames and it learned cats on its own, an early landmark of unsupervised learning. Google X is the trap because the project started there, but the team and the result belong to Brain. Google did not acquire DeepMind until 2014.

text: Which Cologne-based company's neural translation service launched as DeepL Translator in 2017?
explanation: DeepL grew out of the Linguee dictionary team, and its 2017 translator beat Google on blind tests, funded by a wave of press buzz. SAP is the tempting answer as Germany's other software giant, but translation is Cologne's DeepL, not Walldorf's SAP. The company later expanded from translation into its own language models.

text: Which company's 2024 personal-intelligence system splits work between on-device models and Private Cloud Compute?
explanation: Apple announced Apple Intelligence at WWDC 2024, splitting work between on-device models and Private Cloud Compute. Samsung is the tempting answer because Galaxy AI shipped on phones first, but Apple's system is the one with the Private Cloud name. The long-awaited Siri overhaul was the headline feature.

text: Which company develops the Phi family of small language models?
explanation: Microsoft's Phi models are open-weight and designed to run on phones and laptops, with Phi-1 arriving in June 2023. Google is the tempting answer because it ships Gemma, another open-weight family, but Phi is Microsoft's.

text: Which lab develops the Gemma family of open models?
explanation: Gemma is Google DeepMind's family of source-available models, first released in February 2024 as a lightweight sibling of Gemini. Meta AI is the tempting answer because it also publishes open-weight models, but Llama is Meta's family.

text: Which company created the Granite family of foundation models?
explanation: IBM Research announced Granite in September 2023 for the Watsonx platform, later open-sourcing the code models under Apache 2.0. Oracle is the tempting answer as another enterprise software giant, but Granite is IBM's.

text: Which lab developed the Jamba model family?
explanation: AI21 Labs released Jamba in March 2024 as a hybrid Mamba-transformer mixture-of-experts model with context up to 256,000 tokens. Cohere is the tempting answer as another enterprise-focused lab, but its family is Command.

text: Which lab released the Mixtral mixture-of-experts model?
explanation: Mistral AI released Mixtral 8x7B in December 2023 via a BitTorrent link, a sparse model that beat Llama 70B on many benchmarks. DeepSeek is the tempting answer as another open-weight lab, but its family is DeepSeek.

text: Which lab released the reasoning model DeepSeek-R1?
explanation: DeepSeek, funded by the High-Flyer hedge fund in Hangzhou, released DeepSeek-R1 as an open-weights reasoning model. Alibaba is the tempting answer as another Chinese AI giant, but its family is Qwen.

text: Which Shanghai-based lab is one of China's six AI Tigers and builds the Step models?
explanation: StepFun was founded in Shanghai in April 2023 by former Microsoft engineers and released Step-2, a trillion-parameter model, in 2024. MiniMax is the tempting answer as another Shanghai AI Tiger, but its family is MiniMax.

text: Which Shanghai-based company develops the abab models and the Talkie app?
explanation: MiniMax was founded in December 2021 in Shanghai and built the abab model line plus the Talkie and Hailuo AI apps. StepFun is the tempting answer as another Shanghai lab, but its family is Step.

text: Which Beijing lab was founded by Sogou's former CEO Wang Xiaochuan?
explanation: Wang Xiaochuan founded Baichuan in April 2023 after leaving Sogou, naming it after the phrase 'A Hundred Rivers'. 01.AI is the tempting answer as another Beijing AI Tiger, but that was Kai-Fu Lee's.

text: Which Tokyo-based lab was co-founded by transformer paper co-author Llion Jones?
explanation: Sakana AI was founded in Tokyo in July 2023 by David Ha, Llion Jones and Ren Ito, with Jones being a co-author of Attention Is All You Need. Preferred Networks is the tempting answer as another Japanese AI company, but it is not Sakana's.

text: Which German non-profit created the LAION image datasets used to train Stable Diffusion?
explanation: LAION, short for Large-scale Artificial Intelligence Open Network, is a German non-profit that released LAION-400M and LAION-5B scraped from Common Crawl. EleutherAI is the tempting answer as another open collective, but its focus was language models, not image datasets.

text: Which company acquired the generative AI startup MosaicML in 2023?
explanation: Databricks bought MosaicML for $1.4 billion in June 2023 and folded it into its Data Intelligence Platform. Snowflake is the tempting answer as a rival data platform, but it did not buy MosaicML.

text: DeepSeek is funded by which Chinese hedge fund?
explanation: DeepSeek is unusual in being backed by High-Flyer, a quantitative hedge fund, rather than venture capital. Citadel is the tempting answer as a famous hedge fund, but it has no link to DeepSeek.

text: Mistral AI takes its name from a wind blowing in which country?
explanation: Mistral is named after the mistral, a cold northwesterly wind that blows in southern France. Italy is the tempting answer because the wind also reaches there, but the namesake is French.

text: Which company develops the Hunyuan family of models?
explanation: Tencent, headquartered in Shenzhen, develops the Hunyuan models alongside WeChat and its other products. Baidu is the tempting answer as another Chinese AI giant, but its family is ERNIE.
